title: Book One · Chapter 96: Bo Makes a Bridge
story:
Bo comes to the green gate with Mr Han on Saturday.

Mr Han has a shirt for Mum to mend. Bo has a small bundle of flat sticks. String holds them together.

“Can Ronan come out?” he asks.

Ronan is already at the door.

They may use a dry corner of the yard while the adults talk. The black cat is asleep on the warm wall. It opens one eye when the sticks rattle.

“I am making a bridge,” Bo says.

“For the cat?”

“For these.”

He takes two little stones from his pocket. They are his bridge feet. Between them he lays three sticks. The first bridge falls when he touches it.

Ronan thinks of the boat strips. He offers to hold the sticks while Bo ties them. Bo wants to try a different place for them first.

Ronan sits on his hands. He must ask Bo first. He keeps his hands under him for now.

Bo moves the stones closer. The sticks stay up, but the middle one rolls sideways. Ronan points at it.

“Flat side down.”

“It is already down.”

They turn the stick together. One side is not quite flat. Bo chooses another. The bridge now carries one pebble from the yard.

How many stones can it carry? Ronan wants to test it. Bo wants to make the sides look neat. They each speak at the same time.

“My bridge,” Bo says.

Ronan stops. He feels cross for a moment. But Bo is right: it is his bridge.

“May I make a boat to go under it?”

Bo looks at the small gap. “A very low one.”

Ronan fetches a scrap of paper. He folds a flat shape for his boat. Then he pushes it gently across the dry ground. It catches against a bridge foot.

“Your river is rough,” Bo says.

“Your bridge is in it.”

They laugh. Ronan moves the paper by hand. He makes a quiet boat noise. Bo lifts one end of the bridge. Now their bridge can open for boats.

The game lasts longer than the building. They send a leaf cart over the sticks. A tiny twig gets stuck underneath. The cat stands up at last. It steps across their whole river. Then it jumps down from the wall.

“Very large passenger,” Ronan says.

“Did not buy a ticket,” Bo adds.

When Mr Han is ready to leave, Bo begins to untie the sticks. “Can the bridge stay until tomorrow?” Ronan asks.

“I need the sticks at home.”

“Oh.”

Bo hesitates. “You can keep two. Not the flat middle one.”

Ronan accepts the two. He does not call them the bridge. They are pieces from a game they made together.

After the visitors leave, Mum asks him to clear up. Someone could trip over the little stones. He returns the yard pebbles to the edge. Bo left his two bridge stones behind. Ronan folds paper round them and writes Bo's name on it.

Mr Han comes back for them before supper. Ronan hands them over.

“He counted,” Mr Han says.

“So did I.”

That evening, Ronan puts his two sticks beside the school folder. He could make another bridge. He could make a small dock for the wooden boat. That would give it a place to stop. He leaves them loose for now. He has no final plan for them yet. He leaves the sticks apart until he decides.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- bundle＝一捆
- flat side＝平的一面
- dock＝小码头
- trip＝绊倒

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：pebble＝小石头；twig＝小树枝；passenger＝乘客。

## 读句提示

**He must ask Bo first.**

他／必须先问／Bo。再做下一步，不用without asking来浓缩。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan怎样尊重Bo对桥的决定？
2. 他们怎样把不完美的模型变成游戏？
